newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-OGRIN WINS AT TEXAS BY A STROKE, WOODS IS THIRD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-OGRIN WINS AT TEXAS BY A STROKE, WOODS IS THIRD.

text.p: Perennial battler
David Ogrin clinched his first victory in 405 events on the
PGA Tour when he won the $1.2 million LaCantera Texas Open by
one stroke Sunday.
Ogrin, who has lived nearby for a decade, used his
intimate knowledge of the LaCantera course to eke out a
rollercoaster even-par 72.
He tapped in from six inches for a bogey at the last hole
to finish at 13-under 275, one shot ahead of fellow American
Jay Haas (70), whose long birdie chance on the last hole was
short.
Tiger Woods, in only his sixth start as a professional,
continued his phenomenal rise with a 67 to finish third, two
strokes back.
But the day belonged to Ogrin, who won $216,000 and a
prized invitation to next year's Masters, where he has played
only once, in 1984.
"You saw all the home-course advantage today," said Ogrin,
38, who has played LaCantera about 50 times.
"I never thought that mess I threw out there today would
win. Winning at home is a little easier than winning on the
road."
Ogrin's round comprised seven birdies, six pars, four
bogeys and a triple bogey.
He teed off with a three-shot lead, but was level with
Haas after a triple bogey at the par-three sixth, where he
hooked his tee shot into a hazard and had little choice but to
take a penalty stroke.
However, Ogrin roared back with birdies at the next four
holes and stayed ahead until the end, where he was afforded
the luxury of two putts from nine feet for victory.
Ogrin, in his 14th season on tour, rose to 32nd on this
year's money list, while Woods improved to 34th.
Woods, 20, started the day seven strokes off the pace, but
drove his first tee shot into a bush. He took a penalty
stroke, but saved par, and after picking up two birdies on the
front nine, eagled the par-five 10th.
Suddenly Woods, the three-time U.S. amateur champion who
won last week's Las Vegas Invitational barely a month after
turning pro, was in the hunt to win back-to-back events.
He birdied the 14th and 15th holes, but missed a
six-footer for birdie at the 16th, before surrendering any
chance of winning with his lone bogey of the day at the
par-three 17th.
"I never play for second," Woods said. "The idea is to win
the damn thing. I thought I had a good chance and I did. I
just came up a bit short."
Woods then issued an ominous warning to the rest of the
tour when he said he had not been on top of his game.
"I didn't really hit the ball very well this week," he
said. "It's nice when you can get it around and still be in
the hunt when you haven't got your A game. I can still compete
out there when I don't have it."
